purpose: Define, before any word is read out of a dictionary, what a conservative research prompt pack may contain: which twenty words, which consonant opportunities inside them count, which are refused and why, and what the pack may never be used for. The pack is a written list with evidence attached. It records nothing about any speaker, scores nobody and produces no artifact.
what_this_pack_is: Twenty chosen English words, each carrying a British broad transcription in the Montreal Forced Aligner English (UK) dictionary and an Australian tagged pronunciation in Wiktionary.
For each word, every consonant opportunity in it, with its position, its state and, where it is refused, the reason.
A developer research pack for checkpoint 22G, which has nothing to point at until this exists.
what_this_pack_is_not: It is not the active onboarding pronunciation task. The word pack in assessment/pronunciation-research-v1.0.0.json stays empty and awaiting professional review, and this checkpoint does not fill it.

It is not professionally reviewed. Qualified phonetic or speech pathology review, familiarity and cultural review, recorded prompt review and a separate owner approval are all unmet, and are listed as such.
It is not truth about any pronunciation. A lexicon proposes how a word may be said and never observes how anybody said it, which is why all four reference sources keep truth_class unavailable.
It is not a detector, a threshold, a score or a selection. No system is selected, no gate moves and the frozen benchmark and selection record are untouched.

british_reference.role: the expected phone path for the British variety
british_reference.why_this_and_not_the_wikipron_scrape: Checkpoint 22E7 measured both. English (UK) places a post-vocalic rhotic in 0.01 percent of its entries against the scrape's 6.85 percent, and carries 78 phones against the scrape's 239 symbols, because volunteers add loanword pronunciations. The scrape is a coverage and variant supplement and carries a prohibited role that stops it becoming the reference.

australian_overlay.role: the Australian tagged variant set, phonemic transcriptions only
australian_overlay.why_phonemic_only: A transcription in brackets is a narrower claim about one production than a transcription in slashes. The two are different claims and are not pooled.
australian_overlay.pool_size: 5,347 words carrying 11,328 Australian tagged pronunciations, of which 3,166 also carry a British reference. Against a pack of twenty chosen words that is ample by two orders of magnitude.

sources_that_may_not_define_a_target: Any grapheme to phoneme model. No target in this pack is machine generated.
Bookbot, whose claimed Australian provenance was disproved at checkpoint 22E6.
Macquarie, which was never licensed and which the owner decided on 2026-07-28 not to ask for.
Any candidate system's own output. A system may not propose the target it is then measured against.

phoneme_alphabet.why_broad: The protocol makes broad IPA the default research representation, because greater transcription detail reduces transcriber agreement. The aligner writes aspiration, palatalisation, labialisation, dentality and dark l as separate symbols; those are allophonic detail, and the pack normalises them to the phoneme with a written reason for every entry.
phoneme_alphabet.why_consonants_only: Vowel and diphthong judgements are explicitly unavailable in the first measurable scope, and the Australian and British vowel systems differ from the American one far more than the consonants do.
phoneme_alphabet.an_unlisted_symbol_is_an_error: A symbol in either source that the pack's normalisation tables do not name refuses the word. It is never dropped silently.

opportunity_rules.an_opportunity_is: one consonant position in the expected pronunciation of one word
opportunity_rules.alignment: Every documented British form and every documented Australian form of a word must yield a consonant sequence of the same length. If they do not, the word is refused whole, because positions that cannot be aligned cannot be compared.
opportunity_rules.agreement: A position is scorable only where every documented form of both varieties gives the same phoneme in the same context. Any disagreement makes that one position unscorable and leaves the rest of the word intact.

union_rule.statement: The accepted set for a word is the union of its documented British and Australian forms. It is never reduced to one form, and neither form is an error.
union_rule.where_they_disagree: unscorable at that position, recorded as documented_variant_disagreement
union_rule.where_no_australian_entry_exists: The word never enters the pack at all. Carrying a British reference and an Australian tag is a selection requirement, so the case the brief describes cannot arise inside the pack.
union_rule.never: An Australian pronunciation is never averaged with, or subtracted from, a British one. A variety mismatch may be excluded but never subtracted.

variety_sensitive_exclusions.this_list_is_this_project_s_own_construc: No ASHA or Speech Pathology Australia guidance enumerates dialect stable English segments, and the 2026-07-25 review found no ready made Australian and American divergence list anywhere. Every entry below therefore cites evidence recorded inside this repository rather than an external authority, and the list is not claimed to be complete.

rules.applies_to: an expected rhotic with no vowel immediately after it
rules.evidence: Checkpoint 22E8 measured Australian speakers flagged 0.030 more often than the American control on the rhotic under the American reference. The first measurable scope already lists post-vocalic r as unavailable.
rules.note: Under a non-rhotic British reference this opportunity mostly does not exist to begin with, which is exactly the mechanism 22E8 recorded: the repair works by declining to ask rather than by fitting better.

rules.applies_to: an expected t or d with a vowel immediately before and immediately after
rules.evidence: Checkpoint 22E8 measured Australian speakers flagged 0.030 more often on t under the American reference. The protocol names t flapping as an ordinary Australian feature that no automatic method separates from a genuine difficulty at a single opportunity.

rules.applies_to: an expected t with no vowel immediately after it
rules.evidence: The 2026-07-25 owner demonstration recorded at accent-contrast-v1.0.0.json flagged final t on natural Australian speech under an American scorer. The aligner itself writes a glottal stop for many of these positions.

rules.applies_to: an expected l with no vowel immediately after it
rules.evidence: The same owner demonstration flagged dark l, and phone mapping version 1.1.0 recorded that the frozen local model never emits dark l for English at all.

The protocol states that fricatives are not a safe class because the dental fricatives are subject to fronting in Australian and British English and to stopping in other varieties. The aligner's own dictionary carries stopped variants of both.

rules.applies_to: any documented form using a glottal stop
rules.evidence: Glottal variants are explicitly unavailable in the first measurable scope.

rules.applies_to: any documented form using a syllabic consonant at that position
rules.evidence: Reductions and unresolved allophones are explicitly unavailable in the first measurable scope.

word_selection.chosen_by: the repository's engineering work, not by a qualified reviewer
word_selection.why_a_human_chooses: The brief says we choose the words, and the eligible pool is thousands of words wide against a pack of twenty. An automatic ranking would imply a familiarity measurement this project does not hold, so the choice is made openly, with a reason recorded for every word, and the builder then verifies every chosen word against every mechanical rule and fails closed if one does not pass.
requirements_every_chosen_word_must_pass: present in the Montreal Forced Aligner English (UK) dictionary
carrying at least one Australian tagged phonemic Wiktionary pronunciation
every documented form of both varieties parses into the pack's phoneme alphabet
every documented form yields the same number of consonants
an ordinary alphabetic word, not an affix, contraction or aligner token

coverage_requirement.rule: Every consonant the pack probes must appear in at least two distinct word positions, where the eligible pool and ordinary word familiarity permit it. A consonant that cannot meet this must be named with its reason rather than quietly left at one.
coverage_requirement.source: The controlled pronunciation protocol requires covering sounds in more than one context where pack length permits.

declared_shortfalls.reason: English /h/ occurs only in syllable onsets, and the eligible pool offers a single word-medial candidate, adhere, which is not an ordinary everyday prompt. One position is reported rather than forced.
Not probed at all. The eligible pool carries it word-medially in three words and nowhere else, so it cannot meet the two position rule and is excluded rather than reported at one.

sensitive_content_screen.performed_by: the repository's engineering work, not a cultural or clinical reviewer
sensitive_content_screen.this_is_not_the_review_the_protocol_requ: Familiarity and cultural review by qualified people familiar with the supported English varieties remains an unmet activation requirement. This screen is a floor, not that review.

written_word.prompt: the word's ordinary spelling, shown one word at a time

recorded_prompt_alternative.why: No reviewed prompt audio exists, and recording some here would be worse than leaving it empty: a spoken prompt carries the speaker's own variety, so the person would be imitating one accent rather than saying a word. The protocol also requires the recorded prompt to be reviewed and the prompt audio to end before the participant recording begins.

distribution_boundary.why: Wiktionary derived material is CC BY-SA. Share alike attaches when adapted material is distributed, not when it is used internally, so shipping a derived lexicon inside a mobile application would trigger it. This is the standing boundary recorded in the Wiktionary and WikiPron manifests at checkpoint 22E7.
what_stays_private: the full expected phone sequences, vowels included
every documented British and Australian form, verbatim
distribution_boundary.what_is_committed: The twenty words, and for each one the consonant opportunities with their position, context, state and reason. That is the pack's own measurement target rather than a pronunciation dictionary, it carries no vowels, and without it no opportunity could be audited.
